notes: This signal was SYNTHESISED. The emitter and the detector did not run, so nothing here demonstrates that a real feed would have produced this event — only that the evaluator behaves this way when it does.

It says so in its own row: payload.__generator records the rung and the skipped steps. It is NOT marked source='manual' — the engine reserves that for the synchronous enrol endpoint and excludes it from every sweep, so a signal written that way would never be drained at all. `payload ? '__generator'` is how to tell these from real ones.

rows.note: The freshness ladder on 'dev' is a real record of what the real schedules did. This tool never writes into it there — an abstention you see here is the genuine state of that cluster's feeds, which is the only way it is worth anything.

No watermarks were written this run. That does NOT guarantee an abstention: watermarks written by an earlier run stay fresh for 25 hours, so the guards keep judging until the newest one ages out. The Detectors table below reports what each one actually concluded, and an abstention there is the guard refusing to judge a feed it cannot see — not a fault.
